messages.author: 51a6f5eacc9bb449
messages.subject: request tryCatch for `solve` in userGWAS
parts:
Hi there,

I am running userGWAS with ML estimation to obtain chi square statistics for Q SNP analyses. However, I keep running into an issue in which the userGWAS run stops short because of a computationally singular matrix. 

The issue I'm having is that I am running the QSNP analyses in batches of SNPs due to the size of my data. The original multivariate GWAS contained about 6.7 million SNPs. I am currently splitting each chromosome up into many small chunks, but even still, the singular matrix issue causes userGWAS to halt after a few hundred or a few thousand SNPs. I only obtain results for about 450,000 SNPs in the QSNP analysis. I assume the error arises from running 'solve' at various stages of the code.

There could of course be user error somewhere in my setup of the models, but what I would request is a tryCatch addition to the GWAS functions that would allow the GWAS to continue if the S or V matrix with a given SNP added is singular. Right now, the entire process halts if one SNP causes problems, meaning that subsequent SNPs are not analyzed. 

If other solutions exist (besides running one SNP at a time), please let me know! 

Thanks,
Justin

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: request tryCatch for `solve` in userGWAS
parts:
Hi Justin, 

Great suggestion! I've added trycatch for both the commonfactorGWAS and userGWAS for the Q SNP analyses where the solve function is used. I also want to highlight that in the last day the GWAS functions were updated to no longer take output from addSNPs and instead performs the function of addSNPs (combining the sumstats and ldsc output to create the SNP-specific matrices) within the context of the function. The GWAS functions were changed over a year to accept the ldsc and sumstats output directly, but just in case you are still using the addSNPs output I wanted to make sure to flag so you don't end up running into a whole new set of issues. Let me know if you run into any problems!

Best, 
  Andrew
